title: The finite equivariant normalization model of a prescribed separable field extension
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $S$ be a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme, and let a finite group $H$ act on $S$ and $k$ compatibly, allowing nonfaithful actions. Put $K=k(S)$ and let $A_h=(h^{-1})^*$ be the induced left action on $K$. Let $M/K$ be a prescribed finite separable extension. Suppose given a finite group $J$, a surjective homomorphism $\rho:J\to H$, and a homomorphism $\sigma:J\to\operatorname{Aut}(M)$ such that $\sigma_j|_K=A_{\rho(j)}$. Let $a:W\to S$ be the normalization of $S$ in $M$, defined by [def-fin-normalization-extension]. Then $W$ is normal integral projective and of finite type over $k$, its function field is canonically $M$, and $a$ is finite and surjective. There exists a dense open $V\subset S$ such that $a^{-1}V\to V$ is etale. For every nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset S$, its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}\overline B^{\,M}$, with $\overline B^{\,M}$ the integral closure of $B$ in $M$, and its generic fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}M$. There is a $J$-action on $W$ whose generic geometric action is $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma_j^{-1})$ and for which $a\circ j=\rho(j)\circ a$. The action on $k$ is the original one composed with $\rho$, and the induced left field action on $k(W)=M$ is exactly $\sigma$.

Normal means that local rings are integrally closed domains; integral closure consists of elements satisfying a monic polynomial over the base ring. Field, integral scheme, projectivity (a closed embedding in a finite projective space), finite type, finite morphism, surjectivity, etaleness, function field and field extensions use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension] and [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-model-functoriality] to $V=S$, $H=K$ and the prescribed finite extension $M/K$. Its hypotheses require only integrality and finite type over the field, both assumed here. For the very normalization $W$ in the statement it gives normality, integrality, finite type over $k$, the canonical identification $k(W)=M$, finiteness and surjectivity of $a$, and Noetherianity of $S$ and $W$. Apply [lem-fin-finite-over-projective] with its base equal to $\operatorname{Spec}k$, its $T$ equal to our $S$, and $h=a$. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field; this base is affine. The structure morphism $S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is projective in the convention of the cited node: it has the closed immersion into $\mathbf P^N_k$ given by the assumed projectivity of $S$ over $k$, and it is quasi-compact because finite type includes quasi-compactness. Its final clause therefore gives a closed immersion of $W$ into a finite projective space over $k$, precisely the projectivity asserted here.

proof.text: For any nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ in $S$, [def-fin-normalization-extension] gives $a^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $C=\overline B^{\,M}$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], $B$ is a domain with fraction field $K$, and $U$ contains the generic point. The affine fibre-product formula and localization base change identify the generic fibre ring with $C\otimes_B K=(B\setminus\{0\})^{-1}C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], this is the integral closure of $K$ in $M$: localization of $M$ at the nonzero elements of $B$ is $M$ itself. Every element of the finite extension $M/K$ satisfies its monic minimal polynomial over $K$, so that closure is all of $M$. Thus the generic fibre is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}M$, with its specified map to $\operatorname{Spec}K$. The identifications use the inclusions into $M$, so agree for different choices of $U$.

source.place: Tag 0307 (lemma-integral-closure-localize), and Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization); affine generic-fibre interpretation: schemes.tex Tags 01I4 and 01JQ.

proof.text: By the Noetherianity of $S$ from Step 1, $S$ is covered by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ a Noetherian ring; since $S$ is nonempty, choose one such nonempty member $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of this cover. Step 2 applies to it. With fraction field $K$ as in Step 2 and the given finite separable extension $M/K$, [lem-weil-pbc-spread-finite-separable-extension] supplies $0\ne c\in B$ and a finite etale $B[c^{-1}]$-algebra $D$ which is a domain with fraction field the prescribed $M$. Put $V=D_U(c)$ and $P=\operatorname{Spec}D$. Then $V$ is nonempty since it contains the generic point, hence dense in the integral $S$. It is normal because its local rings are the local rings of $S$ at its points. The domain $D$ makes $P$ nonempty and irreducible, hence connected. The supplied map $P\to V$ is finite etale and its function field is $M$ compatibly over $K$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph beginning "A primitive element for K′/K": invert the coefficient denominators and discriminant to get the finite free etale domain. Here the prescribed extension is M/K.

proof.text: Apply [lem-fin-normalization-extends-cover] with $X=S$, the nonempty normal open $V$ of Step 3 and its connected finite etale cover $P$. All its hypotheses were verified in Steps 1 and 3. Since the supplied identification $k(P)=M$ is one of $K$-extensions, its normalization of $S$ in $k(P)$ is our $W$: on each affine chart the two integral-closure subrings in the identified field coincide. The cited theorem identifies $a^{-1}V\to V$ with $P\to V$, proving the required dense-open etaleness. No invariance of this chosen $V$ under a group is asserted or needed.

proof.text: Let $h_j$ denote the automorphism of $S$ given by $\rho(j)$, and give $k$ the corresponding action. Then $j\mapsto h_j$ is an action since $\rho$ is a homomorphism. The compatibility $\sigma_j|_K=(h_{j^{-1}})^*$ says equivalently that $\sigma_j^{-1}|_K=h_j^*$. Thus the semilinear isomorphism clause of [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-model-functoriality], applied to $h_j$ with contravariant field pullback $\sigma_j^{-1}$, gives an isomorphism $b_j:W\to W$ over $h_j$ whose pullback on $M$ is $\sigma_j^{-1}$. Its identity and composition clause gives $b_1=1$ and $b_jb_l=b_{jl}$: contravariantly the composite pulls back by $\sigma_l^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}=\sigma_{jl}^{-1}$. These equations also follow from uniqueness of that compatible lift. Hence the $b_j$ form a $J$-action and $a b_j=h_j a$. This use allows nonfaithful actions and movement of $k$, exactly as the cited statement specifies.

source.place: Tags 035H (definition-normalization-X-in-Y), 035I (lemma-characterize-normalization), 035K (lemma-normalization-localization): semilinear transport and uniqueness as in the cited functoriality node.

proof.text: On the generic fibre the pullback of $b_j$ is $\sigma_j^{-1}$, so its geometric action is $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma_j^{-1})$. The induced left field action is defined using inverse scheme automorphisms: $(b_{j^{-1}})^*=\sigma_{j^{-1}}^{-1}=\sigma_j$. Finally, the $k$-structure of $W$ is the composite through $a$, so $a b_j=h_j a$ and the given compatibility on $S$ imply compatibility on $W$ with the original action on $k$ composed with $\rho$. This proves the last two clauses with precisely the original action convention.
